newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sunday matches stump religious cricketers.
newsitem.headline: Sunday matches stump religious cricketers.

text.p: A team of Australian cricketers must play on Sundays after losing a legal battle in which they had claimed that being forced to play on Sunday amounted to religious discrimination.
"Sunday sport may be a society norm in Australia, but it's not for us," said Chris Hunter, president of the Kyabram United Cricket Club.
"We're not a bunch of gospel-toting, bible-bashing idiots. We're just a bunch of average blokes who do not want to play on the Lord's Day," Hunter told Reuters on Thursday.

But the club, whose membership is drawn from Uniting, Baptist and Assembly of God churches, failed on Wednesday to convince Australia's Anti-Discrimination Tribunal that being ordered to play on Sunday infringed on their religious freedom.
The club has battled the local cricket association in rural Victoria over the issue since their junior side was forced to forfeit a finals appearance on religious grounds 10 years ago.

"The association knew our stand and made a verbal promise not to schedule us for Sunday games, then they didn't honour their promise," said Hunter. "I feel disappointed that our Christian virtue has been just swept aside."
But association vice-president Peter McCarthy said the club was not always as pious as it claimed to be.
"Chris Hunter goes to work on Sundays and goes to watch cricket on Sundays, so why can't he play?" McCarthy asked.
